introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. English Language 2 (0730), June 2019, ADVANCED LEVEL. Paper 2: Section A - Summary and Text Reconstruction; Section B - Composition; Section C - Prescribed Texts. Duration: THREE HOURS.**

Answer BOTH questions in SECTION A and ONE EACH from SECTIONS B and C in the SAME Answer Booklet, beginning each section on a new page. Begin with SECTION A.

Read all instructions on BOTH the question paper and the answer booklet very carefully. Failure to obey these instructions or number your work as on the question paper will cause you to lose marks.

Any unusual mark, sign or unnecessary disclosure considered as an attempt to cheat will earn you a penalty.

In the SUMMARY question, use mainly your own words. Indiscriminate copying of portions of the passage as your answer will earn you no marks.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

A pre-prepared or memorized composition will earn you no marks.
enonce_intro_markdown:
**SECTION B - COMPOSITION (20 marks)**

Mark distribution: Content and Organisation (06 marks); Expression (08 marks); Accuracy (06 marks).

Choose ONE topic to write about from the list below. You are advised to write clearly and effectively, to spell and punctuate correctly, and to ensure that your writing is appropriate in style and content to the topic chosen. Avoid obscene language and do not disclose your identity. You should write between 500 and 550 words.

questions.enonce_markdown: **a)** Write a story which illustrates the expression, "Fire is a good servant, but a bad master".
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Plan**

1. Introduction: the proverb and the narrator's first indifference to it.
2. Pa Tanyi's careful method of using fire (the servant).
3. The nephew's carelessness on a windy afternoon and the spread of the fire (the master).
4. Damage to the village and the old man's lesson.
5. Conclusion: the new rule and the proverb repeated.

**Model composition (534 words)**

Every dry season, the elders of our village in the grassfields repeat the same proverb to the young: "Fire is a good servant, but a bad master." For years I thought it was merely a saying to fill the silence around the evening hearth. It took one terrible afternoon in my fourteenth year to teach me what it truly meant.

Pa Tanyi, my grandfather's closest friend, was the most respected farmer in the village. For forty years he had cleared his land with fire, and in all that time no spark had ever escaped him. His method was almost a ritual. He cut a wide strip of bare earth around the field, waited for a windless morning, warned his neighbours the day before, and stayed at the edge of the flames with a bundle of wet leaves until the last ember had died. "Fire obeys the man who respects it," he used to say, and we listened with the polite boredom of children.

That season, however, Pa Tanyi was ill, and he entrusted the clearing of his farm to his nephew, Ebai, a confident young man who had returned from the city with little patience for old customs. Ebai considered the firebreak a waste of time and the neighbours' warnings a sign of backwardness. At two o'clock on a hot harmattan afternoon, with the grass as dry as paper and a restless wind blowing from the north, he struck a match and lit the field from three sides.

For a few minutes the blaze obeyed him. It crackled through the weeds and left behind a neat black carpet. Then the wind rose. Flames leapt over the thin path that Ebai had trodden, ran into the neighbouring maize, and raced up the hill toward the houses, throwing out burning leaves like a thousand red birds. Smoke blackened the sky. Women dragged children out of their kitchens, men ran with buckets, and the church bell rang a frantic alarm.

I remember standing beside my mother, my eyes stinging, as Mama Fri's coffee trees, planted over twenty years, vanished in a wall of orange. Within two hours the fire had devoured four farms, a granary and, last of all, the roof of Pa Tanyi's own house. The old man stood in the ashes, leaning on his stick, silent. Ebai, his clothes torn and his face grey, knelt before him and wept, unable to say a word.

It was the rain, arriving at nightfall, that finally conquered what human hands could not. The next morning the whole village gathered on the blackened hills. Nobody shouted at Ebai. Pa Tanyi simply said, "The same flame that cooked your food yesterday has eaten our harvest today. It has not changed; only the one who held it has." Then he asked every family to bring a hoe, and together we rebuilt what we could, beginning with the houses of the poorest.

Since then, no one in our village lights a field without a firebreak and a witness. Ebai now teaches the young the method he once despised. Whenever I strike a match, I hear the old man's voice, and I remember that fire is a good servant, but a bad master.

**Marking grid**

| Criterion | Marks | What earns the marks |
|---|---|---|
| Content and Organisation | 6 | Relevant ideas that answer the topic, developed with examples, in clear paragraphs with an introduction and a conclusion |
| Expression | 8 | Varied vocabulary and sentence structures, appropriate style and tone, fluent links between ideas |
| Accuracy | 6 | Correct grammar, tenses, spelling and punctuation |

**Common mistakes**

1. A story that only mentions fire without showing both sides of the proverb (its use and its misuse) or that does not illustrate the expression.
2. A list of events with no build-up, dialogue or feeling, and a change of tense from past to present.

incertitudes: Consigne de la page de garde (règle de choix) : « Answer BOTH questions in SECTION A and ONE EACH from SECTIONS B and C in the SAME Answer Booklet ». Section A obligatoire (aucune règle), Section B : 1 sujet sur 6 (a à f), Section C : 1 question sur 4. Les regles_choix sont identiques dans les 12 fichiers.

Fautes imprimées dans le sujet, laissées telles quelles : titre « SECTION A SUMMERY AND TEXT RECONSTRUCTION » (summary), « for few hours » (Q1), « A this stage », « into the will » (mill), « The stripped cane are then », « out of them » (Q2, forme reconstruite) ; Section C question 2 : « Use any Three prescribed text ».
Le tiret cadratin du passage de résumé (« choice of home - among the stinging tentacles ») est écrit « - » conformément à la règle du projet. Le passage ne porte pas de numéros de ligne imprimés.

Section A : le sujet imprime 30 marks pour la section (15 par question). La répartition des 15 points du résumé n'est pas imprimée : la grille du corrigé est indicative. La reconstruction est comptée à 1 point par blanc (15 blancs), ce qui est une hypothèse ; plusieurs réponses sont acceptables pour certains blancs (voir le corrigé).

Section B : 20 marks (Content and Organisation 6, Expression 8, Accuracy 6), 500 à 550 mots demandés. Points imprimés non corrigés. Compositions modèles : comptes de mots faits par script (de 517 à 534 mots).
